# From SPiCT: North Sea thornback ray

Thornback ray (*Raja clavata*) in Subarea 4 and divisions 3.a and 7.d (North
Sea, Skagerrak, Kattegat and eastern English Channel; rjc.27.3a47d) was
benchmarked at the ICES workshop WKBELASMO with SPiCT (ICES, 2023;
Pedersen and Berg, 2017). This chapter converts the final SPiCT assessment to JABBA3,
introduces the F random walk that JABBA3 uses for SPiCT-like fits and for index
years without catch, adds the production lag and AR(1) process error, compares the result with
the SPiCT assessment, and derives the ICES catch advice.

## The benchmark assessment

The final assessment of WKBELASMO 2023 had:

| Setting | Final SPiCT assessment |
|---|---|
| Removals | 1999–2021 (landings and dead discards; 1999–2008 reconstructed), with twice the catch SD before 2009 (`stdevfacC = 2`) |
| Index 1 (Q14) | NS-IBTS-Q1 and FR-CGFS-Q4 combined, biomass of rays ≥ 30 cm, 1989–2021 |
| Index 2 (Q3) | NS-IBTS-Q3, BTS-Eng-Q3 and BTS-BEL-Q3 combined, biomass ≥ 30 cm, 1991–2021 |
| r prior | 0.15 (CV 0.3) |
| Shape | Schaefer (n = 2) |
| Initial depletion | bkfrac 0.15 (CV 0.5) |
| Process error | sdb 0.07 (CV 0.5) |
| Time step | `dteuler = 1/4` |

`data(rjc)` holds the SPiCT input list of the final assessment (`inp`), the
SPiCT fit as an `FLStockR` (`spict.stk`, from `FLRef::spict2FLStockR(base, rel = TRUE)`)
and the life-history parameters of the benchmark (`info`):

```{r rjc-data}
data(rjc)
str(rjc$inp, max.level = 1)
rjc$info$lh
```

With the spict package installed, the assessment refits with
`spict::fit.spict(rjc$inp)`.

## Conversion

```{r rjc-convert}
xs <- spictinp2jabba3(rjc$inp, stock = "rjc.27.3a47d")
xs$priors
```

The indices start ten years before the catch, so the model years are 1989–2021
as in SPiCT; the catch in 1989–1998 is estimated (next section). The index
observation SD is SPiCT's `sdi[index] * stdevfacI`, with one sdi prior per
index, and the catch SD is `sdc * stdevfacC` (0.2 before 2009, 0.1 after).
The annual model refers the indices to the start of the year; SPiCT uses the
survey timing within the year (Q3 at 0.7).

```{r rjc-fit}
fr <- jabba3(xs$data, xs$priors, xs$model, run = "JABBA3")
fr$pars[c("K", "r", "bkinit", "sdb", "sdi1", "sdi2", "sdf"), c("est", "lci", "uci")]
```

## Special feature: the F random walk

By default JABBA3 is conditioned on catch, as JABBA: the catch of each year
enters the biomass equation, with lognormal catch error when
`catch.error = TRUE`. SPiCT instead models fishing mortality as a random walk in
all years and treats the catch as an observation of it. `jb3_model(frw = )`
chooses between them (chapter *JABBA-like and SPiCT-like set-ups*), and the
SPiCT conversion uses the SPiCT-like `frw = "all"`. With the JABBA-like
`frw = "gaps"`, the random walk is used only where the catch series has gaps or
is shorter than the indices (`jb3_data(catch.gaps = "estimate")`, set here by
the converter):

- **Years with catch** stay catch-conditioned, as before.
- **Years without catch** get a harvest rate $H_t$ as a random effect, and the
  catch follows from it: $\hat{C}_t = H_t K P_t$.
- **The random walk** links the harvest rates on the log scale,
  $\log H_t \sim N(\log H_{t-1}, \sigma_F^2)$, for every step that involves a
  year without catch. The walk is therefore anchored to the harvest rate implied
  by the first observed catch (1999 here, $H = C/(K P)$), and the index
  information on biomass in 1989–1998 informs the catch in those years.
- $\sigma_F$ has the prior `jb3_priors(sdf = )` (median 0.3, log-SD 0.5 by
  default; a SPiCT `logsdf` prior is carried over).
- With `frw = "all"` (the conversion here) the random walk applies to all
  years. $\sigma_F$ is then also informed by the years with catch, which
  tends to shrink it and to smooth F through the gaps, and the smooth F
  together with the catch informs the scale (K).

`jbplot_catcherror()` shows the observed catch (1999–2021) against the
estimated catch over all model years. The years without catch are shaded: the
catch there is predicted from the random walk and the biomass, and its
uncertainty narrows towards the first observed catch.

```{r rjc-catch, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5.5}
jbplot_catcherror(fr)
```

## Alternative runs: catch-conditioned, lag and AR(1)

Two alternatives to the converted run: the JABBA-like catch-conditioned
dynamics (`frw = "gaps"`), and the protocol for process error of JABBA3, a production lag at
the age at maturity with AR(1) process deviations. Age at maturity follows from
the benchmark growth parameters and the length at 50% maturity (73.7 cm), and
the AR(1) persistence is the default $\rho = 0.75$:

```{r rjc-alt}
fa <- update(fr, model = list(frw = "gaps"), run = "Catch-conditioned (gaps)")
lh <- rjc$info$lh
amat <- round(lh[["t0"]] - log(1 - lh[["L50"]]/lh[["Linf"]])/lh[["k"]])
amat
fl <- update(fr, model = list(lag = amat, rho = 0.75), run = "Lag 6 + AR(1)")
```

```{r rjc-alt-plot, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 6.5}
jabbaplot3(list(JABBA3 = fr, `Catch-conditioned (gaps)` = fa, `Lag 6 + AR(1)` = fl),
           bthr = NULL, blim = NULL, panels = c("Catch", "F/Fmsy", "B/Bmsy", "procdev"))
```

Terminal status (2021) of the three runs:

```{r rjc-status}
st <- function(f){ x <- f$ts[f$ts$year == 2021 & f$ts$quant %in% c("B/Bmsy", "F/Fmsy"), ]
  stats::setNames(sprintf("%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", x$est, x$lci, x$uci), x$quant) }
noquote(t(sapply(list(JABBA3 = fr, `Catch-conditioned (gaps)` = fa, `Lag 6 + AR(1)` = fl), st)))
```

The converted run reproduces the SPiCT perception: depleted in the 1990s, F
below $F_{MSY}$ since the mid-2000s and a rebuilding stock close to $B_{MSY}$
in 2021 ($B/B_{MSY}$ 0.99 and $F/F_{MSY}$ 0.35, against 1.03 and 0.36 in SPiCT
at the start of 2021), with K close to SPiCT's (148,000 t against 138,000 t).
K is 52 × the maximum catch, so `jabba3()` warns that it lies above the
plausibility bound (24 ×) for this r; a slow-growing ray can be that large
relative to its catch, and SPiCT agrees, so the warning is noted here. The
catch-conditioned run puts K higher still (78 × max catch) and F lower
($F/F_{MSY}$ 0.28): without the random walk the scale is less constrained by
the catch. With the lag
and AR(1) process error, the process deviations become persistent (below
average production in the 1990s, above average from the mid-2000s, when the
stock rebuilt), status is slightly higher, and the intervals are wider: the
persistence of the production anomalies shows as uncertainty.

## Comparison with the SPiCT assessment

`jb3_FLStockR()` converts a JABBA3 fit to an `FLStockR` with posterior draws.
`jbplot_advice()` takes `FLStock`/`FLStockR` objects as well as fits, so the
lag + AR(1) run can be shown with the SPiCT assessment as an `FLStocks` (or a
list mixing fits and stocks). The SPiCT `FLStockR` holds the estimated
trajectory only, so the intervals are shown for JABBA3. The lag + AR(1) run
follows the SPiCT $B/B_{MSY}$ trajectory closely:

```{r rjc-advice, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 3.8}
stks <- FLCore::FLStocks(`JABBA3 lag 6 + AR(1)` = jb3_FLStockR(fl, ndraws = 1000), SPiCT = rjc$spict.stk)
jbplot_advice(stks, colours = c("dodgerblue", "black"), ncol = 3)
```

The same with `FLRef::plotAdvice()`, with the colours set manually:

```{r rjc-advice-flref, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 4.5, eval = requireNamespace("FLRef", quietly = TRUE)}
FLRef::plotAdvice(stks, ncol = 3, type = "spm") +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = c("dodgerblue", "black")) +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = c("dodgerblue", "black"))
```

## ICES catch advice: HCR and catch fractiles

ICES advice for stocks assessed with surplus production models follows a fixed
routine (as for SPiCT stocks; the WKBELASMO forecast used it with SPiCT).
`jb3_advice()` runs it in one call:

| Step | What happens | `jb3_advice()` |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Intermediate year | From the last assessment year (2021), the stock is projected to the advice year with status quo F (mean of the last 3 years) | `imp.years = 1`, `imp = "Fsq"` |
| 2. Harvest control rule | In the advice year (2023), the ICES MSY hockey-stick rule $F = F_{MSY} \times \min(1, B/B_{trigger})$, with $B_{trigger} = 0.5\,B_{MSY}$, is applied to each draw of $B/B_{MSY}$ at the start of the year: this gives the distribution of the catch in the advice year | `ftgt = 1`, `btrigger = 0.5` |
| 3. Catch fractile | The advised catch is a lower percentile of that distribution: the 35th percentile in the ICES advice rule, a lower one (15th or 25th) where status is uncertain | `fractiles = c(0.35, 0.25, 0.15)` |
| 4. Advice table | Each advised catch is projected: F in the advice year, $B/B_{MSY}$ at the start of 2024 and the probability of falling below $B_{lim} = 0.3\,B_{MSY}$ (the precautionary check: at most 5%) | `blim = 0.3` |

The assessment of 2022 uses data up to 2021, so there is one intermediate year
(2022) before the advice year (2023). Other catch options, such as the status
quo catch and a 20% increase (two of the WKBELASMO scenarios), are added with
`catch`. The advice is derived for the converted run and for the lag + AR(1)
run:

```{r rjc-ices-advice}
csq <- mean(tail(fr$data$catch, 2))          # average removals 2020-2021
opts <- c(`Status quo catch` = csq, `Status quo catch +20%` = 1.2*csq)
adv0 <- jb3_advice(fr, fractiles = c(0.35, 0.25, 0.15), imp.years = 1, catch = opts, ndraws = 4000)
adv  <- jb3_advice(fl, fractiles = c(0.35, 0.25, 0.15), imp.years = 1, catch = opts, ndraws = 4000)
adv
```

The two runs side by side:

```{r rjc-ices-compare}
cmp <- function(a, f){
  tb <- a$table; r <- function(b) tb[tb$Basis == b, ]
  fmt <- function(b) sprintf("%s (F/Fmsy %.2f)", format(round(r(b)[[2]]), big.mark = ","), r(b)[[3]])
  c(`B/Bmsy 2021` = sprintf("%.2f", f$ts$est[f$ts$quant == "B/Bmsy" & f$ts$year == 2021]),
    MSY = format(round(f$refpts["MSY", "est"]), big.mark = ","),
    `CV of the 2023 catch under the HCR` = sprintf("%.2f", stats::sd(log(a$catch))),
    `Median catch 2023` = format(round(stats::median(a$catch)), big.mark = ","),
    `35th percentile (ICES advice)` = fmt("HCR, 35th percentile"),
    `25th percentile` = fmt("HCR, 25th percentile"),
    `15th percentile` = fmt("HCR, 15th percentile"),
    `P(B 2024 < Blim) at the 35th` = sprintf("%.1f%%", r("HCR, 35th percentile")$`P(B<Blim)`))
}
knitr::kable(cbind(JABBA3 = cmp(adv0, fr), `Lag 6 + AR(1)` = cmp(adv, fl)))
```

For the lag + AR(1) run: the distribution of the advice-year catch under the
HCR, with the median and the fractiles,

```{r rjc-ices-catch, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
jbplot_advicecatch(adv)
```

the forecast of the catch options (`adv$options`, a `jb3_fwd()` projection),

```{r rjc-ices-forecast, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 5}
jbplot_projection(adv$options, nyears = 10)+ ggplot2::facet_wrap(~quant, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3)
```

and the advice table (`adv$table`):

```{r rjc-ices-table}
knitr::kable(adv$table)
```

What the comparison shows:

- **Lag + AR(1) gives the more precautionary advice, although it estimates the
  stock slightly higher.** Two effects lower the advice: MSY is lower, and the
  forecast catch is much less certain. The persistent process deviations carry
  into the forecast years, so the CV of the advice-year catch nearly doubles.
- **The fractile takes a larger cut where the uncertainty is larger.** The 35th
  percentile is about 93% of the median catch in the converted run and about
  85% with lag + AR(1); the 15th percentile about 82% and 66%. The fractile
  acts through the uncertainty, not the point estimate, which is how the rule
  is meant to work.
- **The SPiCT advice lies between the two runs.** WKBELASMO gave 8051 t at the
  35th percentile (F/Fmsy 0.92, B/Bmsy 1.14 at the start of 2024), 7074 t at
  the 15th percentile and 3441 t for a 20% increase on the realised removals.
  The converted run gives about 8,500 t and the lag + AR(1) run about 6,800 t
  at the 35th percentile.
- **With the uncertainty modelled, a very low fractile may be overly
  cautious.** Allowing for persistence widens the forecast uncertainty, and with
  a fixed fractile that turns directly into precaution, so a 15th percentile on
  top of it lowers F to about 0.65 $F_{MSY}$.
